"High Court judges retire at the age of (A) ______ years. Disputes between the Union and a state go directly to the (B) ______."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why is the Supreme Court called the guardian of the Constitution? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) 62 (ii) Supreme Court (iii) (1) It interprets the Constitution finally. (2) It can strike down laws and actions that violate the Constitution.
items.markingKey: (i) 62 – 1 mark. (ii) Supreme Court – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) It interprets the Constitution finally. (2) It can strike down laws and actions that violate the Constitution.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False. If false, correct it: Free legal aid for the poor is a directive under Article 44.
items.answer: False. Free legal aid for the poor is a directive under Article 39A.
items.markingKey: False (½ mark); correction: '39A' in place of '44' (½ mark). Free legal aid for the poor is a directive under Article 39A.

items.stem:
(a) Sneha lost a property case in the district court. Trace the path her case can take if she is not satisfied, and explain why this system is useful. (3 marks)
(b) Why is the Indian judiciary called an integrated judiciary? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) She can appeal to the High Court of her state. (2) If still not satisfied, she can appeal to the Supreme Court. (3) Appeals allow mistakes of lower courts to be corrected. (b) (1) All courts form a single pyramid with the Supreme Court at the top. (2) Decisions of higher courts are binding on lower courts.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) She can appeal to the High Court of her state. (2) If still not satisfied, she can appeal to the Supreme Court. (3) Appeals allow mistakes of lower courts to be corrected. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) All courts form a single pyramid with the Supreme Court at the top. (2) Decisions of higher courts are binding on lower courts.

items.stem:
Read the revision note prepared by a Class 8 student on "Need for an independent judiciary and the rule of law" and answer the questions that follow.
"The salaries of Supreme Court judges cannot be (A) ______ during their term, except in a financial emergency. A judge of the Supreme Court can be removed only by (B) ______ by Parliament."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why must the judiciary be independent? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) reduced (ii) impeachment (iii) (1) So that judges can decide cases fairly without pressure from politicians. (2) So that it can protect citizens' rights even against the government.
items.markingKey: (i) reduced – 1 mark. (ii) impeachment – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) So that judges can decide cases fairly without pressure from politicians. (2) So that it can protect citizens' rights even against the government.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Only the victim can file a Public Interest Litigation.
Reason (R): PIL was introduced to help people who could not approach courts on their own.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false – any public-spirited person can file a PIL; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False: Judges of the Supreme Court retire at the age of 65 years.
items.answer: True
items.markingKey: True. Judges of the Supreme Court retire at the age of 65 years.

items.stem: Which term is used for free legal advice and a lawyer provided to people who cannot afford them?
items.answer: Legal aid
items.markingKey: (d) Legal aid: free legal advice and a lawyer provided to people who cannot afford them.
options: Original jurisdiction
Impeachment
Rule of law
Legal aid

items.stem: Which of the following correctly describes 'High Court'?
items.answer: The highest court at the level of a state
items.markingKey: (d) 'High Court' means the highest court at the level of a state; the other options describe other terms of this chapter.
options: Division of the work of government among the legislature, the executive and the judiciary
The power of a higher court to hear appeals against decisions of lower courts
Cases waiting in courts for a decision
The highest court at the level of a state

items.stem:
Match Column A with Column B and choose the correct option.
Column A:
1. Writ
2. Legal aid
3. Lok Adalat
4. Mandamus
Column B:
(p) A formal order of a court directing someone to do or not to do something
(q) Free legal advice and a lawyer provided to people who cannot afford them
(r) A "people's court" where disputes are settled by compromise, with no court fee and no appeal
(s) A writ commanding a public official to perform a duty
items.markingKey: (d) Writ – a formal order of a court directing someone to do or not to do something; Legal aid – free legal advice and a lawyer provided to people who cannot afford them; Lok Adalat – a "people's court" where disputes are settled by compromise, with no court fee and no appeal; Mandamus – a writ commanding a public official to perform a duty.

items.stem:
Match Column A with Column B and choose the correct option.
Column A:
1. Original jurisdiction
2. Writ
3. Supreme Court
4. District court
Column B:
(p) The main court of a district, headed by a District Judge
(q) The power of a court to hear certain cases directly, such as disputes between the Union and states
(r) A formal order of a court directing someone to do or not to do something
(s) The highest court of India, located in New Delhi
items.markingKey: (a) Original jurisdiction – the power of a court to hear certain cases directly, such as disputes between the Union and states; Writ – a formal order of a court directing someone to do or not to do something; Supreme Court – the highest court of India, located in New Delhi; District court – the main court of a district, headed by a District Judge.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False: In a PIL, even a letter addressed to the court can be treated as a petition.
items.answer: True
items.markingKey: True. In a PIL, even a letter addressed to the court can be treated as a petition.

items.stem: Choose the correct option to complete the statement: High Courts can issue writs under Article ______.
items.markingKey: (d) High Courts can issue writs under Article 226.

items.stem:
Read the revision note prepared by a Class 8 student on "Access to justice" and answer the questions that follow.
"The decision (award) of a Lok Adalat is final and (A) ______ appeal can be made against it. Lok Adalats were given legal status by the Legal Services Authorities Act of (B) ______."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why is it said that "justice delayed is justice denied"? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) no (ii) 1987 (iii) (1) A decision that comes after many years may be of little use to the victim. (2) Undertrials may spend years in jail before their case is decided.
items.markingKey: (i) no – 1 mark. (ii) 1987 – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) A decision that comes after many years may be of little use to the victim. (2) Undertrials may spend years in jail before their case is decided.
